title: Great River Road (Wisconsin)
direction: The Wisconsin section of the Great River Road, running south along the Mississippi from Prescott to the Illinois line.

sources.driveTimes: OSRM (router.project-osrm.org), OpenStreetMap data, computed at build time; excludes stops and traffic

moments.title: Lake Pepin
moments.text: The river spreads into a lake several miles wide. Pull-offs near Maiden Rock and Stockholm look straight across it.

photo.title: Lake Pepin (Mississippi River) Bluffs, Wisconsin (31646662248).jpg
photo.alt: Wooded bluffs along the shore of Lake Pepin on the Mississippi.
photo.author: Tony Webster from Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States

moments.title: Alma
moments.text: A narrow town squeezed between the bluff and the river, with a lock and dam at its edge.

photo.title: Lock and Dam No. 4 2021-02-27.jpg
photo.alt: Lock and Dam No. 4 across the Mississippi at Alma, with the bluff beyond.
photo.author: August Schwerdfeger

moments.title: Perrot State Park
moments.text: Trails near Trempealeau climb the bluffs above the confluence of the Trempealeau and Mississippi rivers.

photo.title: PerrotStateParkWisconsinTrempealeauMountain.jpg
photo.alt: Trempealeau Mountain rising from the river backwaters at Perrot State Park.
photo.author: Royalbroil

moments.title: Prairie du Chien
moments.text: One of the oldest European settlements on the upper Mississippi, near where the Wisconsin River meets it.

stretches.title: Along Lake Pepin
stretches.line: The river widens into Lake Pepin beside the road.

stretches.title: Lock and dam towns
stretches.line: River towns between the bluffs, with locks on the Mississippi.

stretches.title: Driftless bluffs
stretches.line: Bluffs and backwaters in the unglaciated Driftless Area.

stretches.title: South to Potosi
stretches.line: The southern end of the Wisconsin section.
